top_news.title: ArXiv caps submissions at two per month as AI paper flood overwhelms the preprint server
top_news.dek: ArXiv is implementing a two-submission-per-month limit to combat a surge in AI-generated papers that has overwhelmed volunteer moderators.
top_news.brief: Starting October 1, 2026, ArXiv will restrict users to two submissions per calendar month. The platform has seen monthly submissions exceed 40,000, with the cs.AI category growing sixfold in two years. The policy aims to reduce low-quality volume while maintaining the existing cap of three active submissions at any given time.

top_news.title: 500B Tokens Later: Letting AI Agents Decompile a First-Person Shooter
top_news.dek: A technical case study explores using AI agent orchestration to achieve a feature-complete decompilation of a first-person shooter.
top_news.brief: The project focused on optimizing AI infrastructure and orchestration to handle the massive token requirements of decompiling a complex game. The author emphasizes that the effort was less about the specific game and more about the practical challenges of scaling AI agents for large-scale, stable code reconstruction.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram of AI agent orchestration for code decompilation

top_news.title: Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation
top_news.dek: New research suggests that byte-level language models can outperform traditional subword tokenizers as parameter counts scale.
top_news.brief: The paper challenges the necessity of explicit tokenizers, demonstrating that standard flat Transformers can process raw byte sequences efficiently. While byte sequences are longer, the study indicates that scaling parameter sizes allows models to develop emergent abstractions that surpass the performance of subword-based architectures.
top_news.image_alt: Comparison chart of byte-level vs subword model performance

top_news.title: Agents - Cloudflare API MCP server serves Cloudflare skills
top_news.dek: Cloudflare has released an MCP server that allows AI agents to discover and execute Cloudflare skills directly.
top_news.brief: The Cloudflare API MCP server now supports the 'Skills over MCP' extension. By adding the provided endpoint to a compatible MCP client, developers can list and interact with Cloudflare skills, enabling agents to perform tasks directly through the Cloudflare ecosystem.
